quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle symbol is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: Do highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze before regular roads because they are suspended in the air. Drive slowly and carefully on bridges in freezing temperatures.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about upcoming railroad crossings. Use extra caution when you see this sign.

questions.question: Is having a driver license a requirement, privilege, or right?

options.text: A requirement.
A privilege.
A right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must drive safely. If you abuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the bridge ahead is narrow. It may be too narrow to safely pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: Is a driver license a right or a privilege?

options.text: A right, not a privilege.
A privilege, not a right.
A requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege that you must earn and keep. It is not a right.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far a vehicle needs to stop?

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What is most important when managing speed on curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's weight and momentum can make it hard to turn. Slow down before entering a curve to keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, look for another train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: On an interstate, how do you avoid traffic from on-ramps on your right?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead on the right, move to the left lane when it is safe. This gives merging traffic room to enter.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll toward the side of the road and away from traffic.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without interfering with other traffic.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process per hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
One alcoholic drink an hour.
Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How quickly alcohol affects you depends on the amount you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: When should you increase your distance from the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly, as this could cause a crash.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the wheel in the direction you want the car to go. Once the car straightens out, turn the wheel the other way.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers should then go in the order they arrived at the intersection.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for one hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt up to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat and water together bring more oil to the surface.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for hazards. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Scan the road ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and then:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again in case you missed any vehicles.
